record.original_question: For n > 39, is it true that the number of conjugacy classes in the symmetric group Sn of degree n is never a divisor of the order of Sn? In other words, is it true that, for n > 39, the number p(n) of integer partitions of n is never a divisor of n!?

evidence.quote: For n > 39, is it true that the number of conjugacy classes in the symmetric group Sn of degree n is never a divisor of the order of Sn? In other words, is it true that, for n > 39, the number p(n) of integer partitions of n is never a divisor of n!?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let p(n) denote the number of integer partitions of n, equivalently the number of conjugacy classes of the symmetric group S_n of degree n (which has order n!). Prove or disprove: for every integer n > 39, p(n) does not divide n!.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a new problem in the 2026 Kourovka Notebook collection of open problems in group theory. No published resolution was found in the search; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Kourovka Notebook problems concerning conjugacy classes
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of related Kourovka notebook problems on conjugacy class counts in finite groups; no resolution of the p(n) | n! divisibility question appears.
status_evidence.claim: No published solution to the divisibility problem was located.
